GB.intro: The UK uses the +44 calling code. UK numbers are often written with a leading 0 domestically (the trunk prefix). When calling the UK from abroad, you typically drop that leading 0 and dial +44 instead.

emergencyNumbers.notes: 999 and 112 both connect to the UK emergency services.

nonEmergencyNumbers.notes: 111 is the NHS non-emergency medical number. 101 is the non-emergency number for police (UK).

tips: Domestic UK format often starts with 0 (e.g. 020…, 07…). International format typically removes that 0.
UK mobile numbers usually start with 07 domestically; from abroad that becomes +44 7…
If you’re calling from a mobile, using +44 is the simplest option (no need to know your exit code).
commonMistakes: Dialling +44 0… (keeping the domestic 0 after +44) — this often fails.
Mixing spaces/punctuation into a tel: link instead of a clean E.164 number.

faqs.q: Do I drop the leading 0 when calling the UK internationally?
faqs.a: Usually yes. The leading 0 is a domestic trunk prefix and is typically omitted when dialling from abroad.

US.intro: The United States uses calling code +1 (NANP). +1 is shared across multiple countries/territories, so the area code is essential for identifying the destination.

emergencyNumbers.notes: 911 is the standard emergency number in the United States.

tips: US numbers are commonly written as (AAA) BBB-CCCC. In international/E.164 format this becomes +1AAABBBCCCC.
+1 is shared (NANP). If you only have “+1 …” without context, you can’t always infer the country/territory.
For click-to-call links, prefer tel:+1… without spaces for maximum compatibility.
commonMistakes: Assuming +1 always means the USA (it can also be Canada and other NANP regions).
Dropping the area code (required for most calls).

faqs.a: No. +1 is part of the North American Numbering Plan and is shared by multiple countries and territories (including Canada and others).

FR.intro: France uses calling code +33. French numbers are usually written domestically with a leading 0; when calling from abroad, you generally drop that 0 and use +33.

emergencyNumbers.notes: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number; France also uses 15 (medical), 17 (police), and 18 (fire).

tips: Domestic numbers often look like 0X XX XX XX XX. International format commonly becomes +33 X XX XX XX XX.
Using +33 on mobiles is usually the easiest approach (no exit code needed).

faqs.a: Domestically, yes — the leading 0 is common. Internationally, you typically drop it and dial +33 instead.

ES.intro: Spain uses calling code +34. Spanish national numbers are normally dialled after +34 without removing a separate domestic trunk prefix.
tips: A Madrid landline such as 912 34 56 78 becomes +34 912 34 56 78 from abroad.
On a mobile, saving the number in +34 international format makes it easier to use both inside and outside Spain.
Use the complete national number after +34; Spanish geographic numbers do not use a removable leading 0.
commonMistakes: Treating 34 as part of the local number instead of Spain's country calling code.

faqs.q: Do I drop a leading 0 when calling Spain?
faqs.a: Spain does not use a separate domestic trunk prefix 0 for geographic numbers in the same way as many other European countries. Dial +34 followed by the complete national number.

DE.intro: Germany uses calling code +49. German area codes are written with a leading 0 for domestic calls; when calling from abroad, replace that 0 with +49.
tips: A Berlin number written as 030 123456 becomes +49 30 123456 from abroad.
German area codes vary in length, so keep every digit of the area code except its first 0.
Using +49 is usually simpler than entering a separate international exit code on a mobile.
commonMistakes: Dialling +49 0 followed by the area code; the domestic 0 should normally be removed.
Assuming every German area code has the same number of digits.

faqs.q: How do I call a Berlin number from abroad?
faqs.a: Replace Berlin's domestic 030 prefix with +49 30, then dial the subscriber number.

IN.intro: India uses calling code +91. When an Indian landline is written with a domestic leading 0, remove that 0 when using +91.
tips: A Bengaluru landline written as 080 1234 5678 becomes +91 80 1234 5678 from abroad.
For international format, place +91 before the national number and remove a domestic trunk-prefix 0 if one is present.
Keep the area code for landline calls.
commonMistakes: Dialling +91 0 before an Indian area code.
Leaving out the landline area code.

faqs.q: Do I keep 0 before an Indian area code when calling internationally?
faqs.a: Normally no. Remove the domestic leading 0 and use +91 before the area code and subscriber number.

AU.intro: Australia uses calling code +61. Australian landline and mobile numbers begin with 0 domestically; remove that 0 when calling from abroad.
tips: A Sydney landline written as 02 1234 5678 becomes +61 2 1234 5678.
An Australian mobile written as 0412 345 678 becomes +61 412 345 678.
Using +61 is the simplest mobile-friendly format. Australia's legacy international exit code is 0011.
commonMistakes: Dialling +61 0 followed by the Australian number.
Keeping 04 at the start of a mobile number after adding +61; it should normally begin +61 4.

faqs.q: How do I convert an Australian mobile number to international format?
faqs.a: Remove the first 0 from the mobile number and place +61 in front. For example, 0412 345 678 becomes +61 412 345 678.
